articles.title: Blog
articles.contents: Here, I write about interesting areas of biostatistics in a casual tone. This is mainly an exercise for myself, although I would be glad if others learned something interesting here too!

          Bio
          I am a PhD student in biostatistics at the University of
          Bordeaux, France. I work on new methodology for analysing
          high-dimensional biomolecular data in the context of vaccine
          experiments. My research interests include surrogate markers,
          causal inference, non-parametric statistics, prediction, and
          reproducibility problems.
          As a researcher, I highly value clear and intuitive
          scientific communication, whether in my publications,
          conference communications, or teaching.

          Jobs
          
            
        

        
          
      
      
        
          
          Current Offers
          I have no current internship offers. Any new offers will
          appear here. If you are interested in working on similar
          topics, you are welcome to get in touch:
          Email : arthur.hughes@u-bordeaux.fr
          
          
          Past Offers
          
          2025
          
          Evaluation of Approaches for Identifying High-Dimensional
          Individual-Level Surrogate Markers Applied to Vaccinology
          Description: Proposition for a 6 month
          internship for a master’s student, co-supervised by myself and
          Boris Hejblum. The subject of the internship is the comparison
          of methods for identifying individual-level surrogate markers
          of the vaccine response. The project was completed by Master
          student Roaya Jannatipour.
          View
          internship offer
          
          
          Evaluation of Gene Expression as Trial-Level Surrogate
          Markers of Vaccination Across Multiple Settings
          Description: Proposition for a 6 month
          internship for a master’s student, co-supervised by myself and
          Boris Hejblum. The subject of the internship is the evaluation
          of trial-level surrogate markers of the vaccine response using
          our recently developed approach, using meta-analysis tools to
          evaluate the generalisability of signatures across multiple
          clinical trials.
          View
          internship offer
          
          
          
          2024
          
          Evaluating High-Dimensional Surrogate Markers of the
          Yellow Fever Vaccine Response
          Description: Proposition for a 6 month
          internship for a master’s student, co-supervised by myself and
          Boris Hejblum. The subject of the internship was the
          identification and evaluation of high-dimensional trial-level
          surrogate markers of the vaccine response to yellow fever
          vaccination. The project was completed by Master student
          Theodora Georgakopoulou.
          View
          internship offer

          SurrogateRank
          This
          R package implements nonparametric rank-based methods for
          the identification and evaluation of surrogate markers in a
          small sample setting. A tutorial can
          be found here.
          
          
          
          
          
          predictomics
          R package providing a standardised interface for prediction
          tasks in the context of omics data. Not yet available on
          CRAN.

          Teaching
          
            
        

        
          
      
      
        
          
          MSc Public Health Data Science – ISPED, University of
          Bordeaux
          
          Genomics Data : Generation, Management, and Analysis
          2024 – present
          Description: In this 6 hour long course, I
          give an introduction to genomics data, focusing on the
          generation and analysis of transcriptomic data. In particular,
          I discuss
          Quality control, filtration, normalisation, and batch
          effects
          Exploratory analyses : principal component analysis,
          hierarchical clustering algorithms
          Differential gene expression analysis
          
          Slides Download (PDF) Open in
          new tab
          
          
          Practical work
          (questions) Download (.Rmd) Open in
          new tab (.html)
          
          
          Practical work
          (solutions) Download (.Rmd) Open in
          new tab (.html)
          
          
          
          Genomics Data : Supervised Learning for High-Dimensional
          Data
          2024 – present
          Description: In this 6 hour long course, I
          give an overview on supervised learning in the
          high-dimensional setting, focusing on regression tasks. I
          mainly discuss
          Cross-validation for model evaluation and hyperparameter
          tuning
          Regularised methods (ridge, lasso, and elastic net
          regression)
          Latent variable approaches (prinipal component regression,
          (sparse) partial least squares)
          Model interpretability

          Genomics Data : Test Multiplicity
          2024 – present
          Description: In this 3 hour long course, I
          provide an overview of the multiple testing problem in
          high-dimensional settings. In particular, I discuss
          An introduction to frequentist hypothesis testing
          Family-wise error rate and its control (Bonferroni,
          Holm)
          False discovery rate and its control (Benjamini-Hochberg,
          Benjamini-Yekutieli)

          Core Principles of Epidemiology
          2024 – 2025
          Description: In this 6 hour long course, I
          give an introduction to epidemiology, discussing
          Measures of association
          Study design
          Diagnostics (sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV)
          Causality, types of bias, and directed acylic graphs
